th 07/Dated: 10 December, 2024 I.A. No. 12173 of 2024:
1.

The instant interlocutory application has been filed under Section 430 (1) of the
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 on behalf of appellant, for suspension of
sentence in connection with judgement of conviction dated 29.11.2022 and order of
sentence dated 30.1.2022 passed by the learned Additional Sessions
Judge-I-cum-Special Judge (Pocso) Lohardaga passed in Special Pocso Case No.
10 of 2019 arising out of Lohardaga P.S. Case No. 112 of 2019, whereby and
whereunder, the appellant has been convicted under Sections 365/366A/376 of Ipc
and under Section 4 of Pocso Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment
for five years under Section 365 Ipc along with fine of Rs.5000/-, rigorous
imprisonment for seven years under Section 366A Ipc and rigorous imprisonment
for 20 years under Section 376(1) Ipc along with fine of Rs.20,000/-.

2.

It has been contended on behalf of the learned counsel for the appellant that it is a case where the appellant has falsely been implicated because there is contradiction in the testimony of the witnesses.
3.

It has also been submitted that even there is contradiction in the version of the victim if it will be taken into consideration by making comparative assessment of the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and the testimony recorded in course of the trial.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant, based upon the aforesaid ground, has submitted that it is a fit case for suspension of sentence.
5. While on the other hand, Mr. Shiv Shankar Kumar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent- State has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence.

6. It has been contended by referring to the testimony of the victim who has supported the prosecution version as also the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
7.

It has further been submitted that the victim since is minor and has stated in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that she is carrying three months of pregnancy and that is the reason she wants to live along with the present appellant which itself clarifies that the victim has also supported the prosecution version and the same has been deposed in the testimony, therefore,
it is not a fit case for suspension of sentence.

8. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties, gone across the finding recorded by the learned trial court in the impugned judgment as also gone through the testimony of witnesses as available in the lower court record and the exhibits available therein.

9. This Court in order to appreciate the argument advanced on behalf of the parties has gone through the First Information Report, statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. and the testimony of the victim.

10. It is evident from the statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. where the version in the FIR has been fully supported stating inter alia therein that the victim is carrying three months pregnancy and that is the reason she wants to live along with the present appellant.
11. It has also been recorded therein that if the said thing of carrying three months pregnancy will come into the knowledge of her parents, then she would be killed.
The same version has come in the testimony of the victim.

12. The victim admittedly is minor as per the conclusive finding arrived at by the learned trial court regarding the age and as such, this Court is of the view that even though the victim wants to live Suraj @ Rahman Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95720913/
2 along with the present appellant, the same cannot dilute the offence as stipulated under Section 4 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: 13. This Court, considering the aforesaid fact, is of the view that the present interlocutory application is not fit to be allowed.
14. Accordingly, the instant interlocutory application being I.A. No. 12173 of 2024 stands dismissed.

15. It is made clear that any observation made hereinabove will not prejudice the case on merit,
since, the criminal appeal is lying pending before this Court for its consideration.
(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Navneet Kumar, J.) Saurabh/-
